structureFindings.title: No skip link to bypass the header/tab bar before main content
structureFindings.description: There is no skip-to-main-content link anywhere in the app (grep for skip-link patterns across src/, index.css, App.css, globals.css, and main.tsx returns nothing). structureFindings.title: Collapsed-mode tabpanels reference nonexistent tab ids (dangling aria-labelledby)
structureFindings.wcag: 1.3.1 Info and Relationships (A); 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (A)
structureFindings.description: Every tab panel is hard-wired to a tab id, e.g. aria-labelledby="tab-weather" (App.tsx:590; the same pattern on the panels at lines 905, 926, 949, 966, 983, 1000, 1024, 1052, 1071). On narrow screens TabNav swaps the tab bar for a dropdown (TabNav.tsx:69-73), and the elements carrying id="tab-<id>" then exist only while the dropdown menu is open (the role="option" buttons, TabNav.tsx:298). With the menu closed — the normal state — all ten role="tabpanel" regions have aria-labelledby pointing at ids that are not in the DOM, so assistive technology gets unnamed tabpanels, and the tab/tabpanel relationship (aria-controls from options that are not tabs, panels with no tablist) is structurally broken in this mode. The dropdown's aria-activedescendant="tab-<activeTab>" (TabNav.tsx:269) also duplicates DOM focus already placed on the options, and the panels' aria-controls counterparts are listbox options, not tabs.
structureFindings.evidence: App.tsx:588-590 `role="tabpanel" id="panel-weather" aria-labelledby="tab-weather"`; TabNav.tsx:69-73 `collapsed ? <TabDropdown .../> : <TabBar .../>`; TabNav.tsx:297-298 `role="option" id={`tab-${item.id}`}` rendered only when `open`.
structureFindings.suggestedFix: Give panels a mode-independent name: replace aria-labelledby with a static aria-label per panel (e.g. aria-label="Weather"), or render the panels' role="tabpanel" only when the desktop tablist is present and use plain labeled regions in collapsed mode. Drop aria-activedescendant from the dropdown listbox since focus moves to the options directly.

structureFindings.title: Document title is static; active view is never reflected in the page/window title
structureFindings.description: The title is "SnowRaven" (index.html:7) and nothing in src/ ever writes document.title (grep finds no occurrences); the Tauri window title is likewise static (src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:14). Because the app is a true single page with an in-page tab widget and no routing (no pushState/hash/router anywhere), the static title technically satisfies 2.4.2. But with ten distinct views (Weather, Species Detail, Map Explorer, Statistics, Settings, …), updating the title on tab change would aid orientation for screen-reader users, browser-tab/window switchers, and history — standard SPA practice.
structureFindings.suggestedFix: On tab change in App.tsx, set document.title = `${activeLabel} — SnowRaven` (a small useEffect keyed on activeTab); this also updates the desktop window title in Tauri.

structureFindings.title: External links open new windows without any indication (inconsistent across the app)
structureFindings.description: 43 target="_blank" anchors exist across ~20 component files; only two indicate the behavior — App.tsx:748 and App.tsx:898 use "(opens in new tab)" in aria-label. All others give no warning, including every link in the Help documentation (HelpDocs.tsx:61 renders all HELP.md links with target="_blank" rel="noreferrer" and no indication), the footer GitHub link (App.tsx:1101-1110), SpeciesLinks.tsx:20/45 (whose aria-labels "View X on eBird" omit it), LifeListTable.tsx media-count links, BirdingStats.tsx checklist/region links (15 instances), Checklists.tsx, MapExplorer.tsx, SpeciesDetail.tsx, NamedBirdRow.tsx, Settings.tsx, WeatherTidePanel.tsx, MediaCommentsSection.tsx, MediaStatsSections.tsx, ChecklistComparer.tsx, SightingsMap.tsx, map/HotspotMarkers.tsx, map/TargetMarkers.tsx, AtlasLayer.tsx, speciesDetail/ui.tsx, CommentText.tsx. Unexpected context changes disorient screen-reader and cognitive-disability users; the app already has the right pattern in two places — it just isn't applied consistently.
structureFindings.evidence: HelpDocs.tsx:61 `<a key={ki++} href={lm[2]} target="_blank" rel="noreferrer"` with no new-window indication; grep shows 43 target="_blank" instances, only App.tsx:748 and App.tsx:898 carry "(opens in new tab)".
structureFindings.suggestedFix: Adopt one shared ExternalA component (or extend SpeciesLinks' pattern) that appends "(opens in new tab)" to the accessible name (visually-hidden span or aria-label suffix) and use it for all target="_blank" anchors, including HelpDocs' renderInline link branch.
